(a) Limitation.—Except as provided in subsection (b), none of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2020 for the Air Force may be obligated or expended to procure any F–15EX aircraft, other than the first two prototypes of such aircraft, until a period of 15 days has elapsed following the date on which the Secretary of the Air Force submits to the congressional defense committees a report on the following topics relating to the F–15EX program:
        (1) Acquisition strategy. 
        (2) Cost and schedule estimates. 
        (3) Test and evaluation strategy. 
        (4) Logistics strategy. 
        (5) Post-production fielding strategy.  
    (b) Exception for Long-lead Items.—
        (1) In general.—Notwithstanding subsection (a), the Secretary of the Air Force may use the funds described in paragraph (2) to procure long-lead items for up to six additional F–15EX aircraft beyond the first two prototypes of such aircraft. 
        (2) Funds described.—The funds described in this paragraph are funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2020 for the Air Force for any of the following:
            (A) Research and development, nonrecurring engineering. 
            (B) Aircraft procurement.   
    (c) F–15EX Program Defined.—In this section, the term “F–15EX program” means the F–15EX aircraft program of the Air Force as described in the materials submitted to Congress by the Secretary of Defense in support of the budget of the President for fiscal year 2020 (as submitted to Congress under section 1105(a) of title 21, United States Code).

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the report-and-wait requirement is a procedural check that counts as participation. However, the report goes only to the congressional defense committees, and Congress is inside the federal government. The section otherwise limits the use of funds and defines the F-15EX program; no state, company, expert, or member of the public is consulted, and there is no rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue.
fable.s: until a period of 15 days has elapsed following the date on which the Secretary of the Air Force submits to the congressional defense committees a report

qwen_block.w: This section requires the Secretary of the Air Force to submit a report to congressional defense committees. Congress and its committees are considered inside the federal government. Therefore, this is an intra-governmental notification/reporting requirement, not participation by outside parties.
qwen_block.s: until a period of 15 days has elapsed following the date on which the Secretary of the Air Force submits to the congressional defense committees a report

opus.w: The only procedural step in this section is a report from the Secretary of the Air Force to the congressional defense committees, followed by a waiting period. Both sides of that exchange are inside the federal government. A report-and-wait requirement may look like participation, but it never brings in anyone from outside the government, so it does not count under the definition.
opus.s: until a period of 15 days has elapsed following the date on which the Secretary of the Air Force submits to the congressional defense committees a report on the following topics relating to the F–15EX program
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this is participation, because procurement can't go forward until a report is submitted and a waiting period passes. That fails the definition. The report goes to the congressional defense committees, and Congress is inside the federal government. No state, company, expert, or member of the public is consulted or brought into the decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of the Air Force to submit a report to congressional defense committees. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Reporting to an internal government body does not constitute participation with people outside the government.
qwen_chat.s: until a period of 15 days has elapsed following the date on which the Secretary of the Air Force submits to the congressional defense committees a report on the following topics relating to the F–15EX program
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the report is submitted to "congressional defense committees," this constitutes participation. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress, its committees, and its members are INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, reporting to Congress is intra-governmental communication, not participation with outside parties.
